The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a missile
fired at its airport in the capital of Riyadh on Sunday, but officials say another projectile
hit one of its passenger terminals, setting off a fire. As NPR's Ayyaba Trawi reports,
this comes one day after 13 people were killed and more than 300 others wounded,
including some critically, in Houthi attacks on that same airport.
Saudi Arabia had already suspended flights and operations at Riyadh airport when an
unknown projectile hit one of its passenger terminals for the second day in a row.
Yemen's Houthis have struck Saudi airports four times over the past week,
but Saturday's attacks are the deadliest on the capital Riyadh in more than a decade.
Among those killed was a U.S. citizen.
The Iran-backed group says its attacks are in response to more than 2,000
Saudi airstrikes on Houthi areas in various parts of Yemen in recent weeks.
The group also says it hit an Aramco gas facility and an oil refinery in Saudi
Arabia's eastern province in the past 24 hours. Saudi Arabia has not commented on those attacks.
Ayyaba Trawi and Pierre news, Dubai.
Several states are dealing with flooding and high winds in the aftermath of hurricanes
Issa-Iyas and Rachel and Pierre's Shondali Stuster has more on that story.
The remnants of Issa-Iyas and Rachel now post-tropical cyclones have caused flooding
across the south and west. In North Carolina, there were tornado warnings on Sunday as well
as a high risk of flooding from heavy rains. Rapid river rising is also possible as the system
moves out. A tornado watch is also in effect for parts of southern Virginia through Sunday night.
The National Weather Service says parts of the southwest, including southern California,
could receive up to three inches of rain on Sunday. Forecasters also warned of damaging
winds and life-threatening surf as well as rip currents. Rain is expected to continue
from both Issa-Iyas and Rachel through Monday. Shondali Stuster, NPR News.
Election officials around the country are now urging mail-in voters for the midterm elections
to return their ballots as soon as possible. That's because of changes to the mailing
system in some parts of the country. NPR's Hansi Lo Wong has our reports.
Some post offices now have fewer daily pickups and a different way of processing mail to help
the U.S. Postal Service stabilize its shaky finances. Those changes have raised the risk
of getting your mail-in ballot rejected if you mail it close to Election Day.
About a week before November 3rd, the Postal Service says it plans to speed up ballot deliveries.
Still, a USPS public service announcement says if you're voting by mail, do it early.
We recommend that you mail your completed ballot before Election Day, and at least a week before
the deadline by which your mail-in ballot must be received by your local election office.
Voters with mail-in ballots can also consider returning them at their local election office
or at any available drop boxes. Hansi Lo Wong, NPR News.
I'm Dale Willman, and you're listening to NPR News.
A federal judge has ordered President Trump to cancel any remaining television commercials
paid for with millions of dollars in taxpayer money to promote his political messages.
A coalition challenging the ads called them an illegal use of funds.
The administration has indicated the campaign is coming to an end.
Mathematicians are digging through hundreds of research papers and proofs released by
the company OpenAI earlier this last week, and as NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports,
they've got their work cut out for them.
Among the more than 370 solutions generated by AI was one for a long-standing problem
in algebraic geometry. Daniel Litt of the University of Toronto was initially excited
until he found a sign error that meant it was wrong. OpenAI has now retracted the papers in
question. Litt says he still thinks the AI pushed out many brilliant solutions.
My hope is that we're able to extract interesting ideas and interesting understanding from them,
but that's like a lot of work.
Human mathematicians will have to read thousands of pages of AI-generated
manuscripts to see what they can learn. Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
The Jessica Chastain horror flick Other Mommy landed in the top spot at North American theaters
this weekend, bringing in $27.5 million in ticket sales. It cost just $19 million to make.
Verity continued strong, posting $11.5 million, while Resident Evil finished in third.
The biggest disappointment of the weekend, though, was the social reckoning,
which is Aaron Sorkin's latest. It opened in fifth with just $5.5 million in ticket sales.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
